message.content:
The idea of a “best” movie is always a bit subjective, but there are a few ways to look at it that most people agree on: | Criterion | 2020‑era titles that topped the lists | |-----------|---------------------------------------| | **Critical consensus (Rotten Tomatoes / Metacritic)** | • *The Trial of the Chicago 7* (87 % RT, 78 Metacritic)
• *Soul* (98 % RT, 88 Metacritic)
• *The Invisible Man* (93 % RT, 73 Metacritic) | | **Major awards (Oscars, BAFTA, Golden Globes)** | • *The Trial of the Chicago 7* – Best Original Screenplay (Oscar)
• *Soul* – Best Animated Feature (Oscar)
• *Parasite* – Best Picture (Oscar, though released in 2019) | | **Audience reception (IMDb, Letterboxd)** | • *Soul* (IMDb 8.1)
• *The Invisible Man* (IMDb 7.6)
• *The Last Duel* (IMDb 7.5) | | **Box‑office impact (adjusted for pandemic)** | • *The Invisible Man* – $70 M domestic (highest‑grossing theatrical release of 2020)
• *The Trial of the Chicago 7* – $12 M domestic (strong streaming performance) | ### Why those titles stand out | Title | What made it notable in 2020 | |-------|------------------------------| | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | A courtroom drama that combined sharp political commentary with a tight, fast‑paced script. It was one of the few films that managed to get a theatrical release and a strong streaming presence during the pandemic. | | **Soul** | Pixar’s first adult‑oriented feature that blended heartfelt storytelling with a unique take on the afterlife. It won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature and was praised for its music, visuals, and philosophical depth. | | **The Invisible Man** | A modern horror‑thriller that re‑imagined the classic story with a feminist twist. It performed exceptionally well on streaming platforms and earned a solid critical reputation. | | **Parasite** | Though released in 2019, it was the first non‑English film to win Best Picture at the Oscars in 2020, cementing its place as a landmark film of the decade. | ### Bottom line If you’re looking for a 2020 film that received the most critical acclaim and award recognition, *The Trial of the Chicago 7* and *Soul* are the front‑runners. If you’re more interested in audience popularity or box‑office success, *The Invisible Man* and *Parasite* (for its Oscar win) are strong contenders. Ultimately, the “best” film will depend on whether you value critical praise, awards, audience enjoyment, or cultural impact.
